newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle sell $69, up $2 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle sell $69, up $2 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle near midday Tuesday sold at $69.00 per cwt, up $2.00 from the bulk of last week's trade, feedlot sources said.
About 1,000 head total had sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and in Kansas, but numbers were growing as the trade turns more active, sources said.
As trading escalated, talk surfaced that some cattle feeders would pass bids of $69.00 and hold out for $70.00, several sources said.
"Now that bids are at $69.00, the question will be how many will sell at that level," a Kansas source said.
Gains were tied to strong beef demand last week that resulted in the second highest weekly beef movement this year and outlooks for ongoing strength this week, sources noted.
At midday, beef prices were again quoted higher, up $1.63 to $2.29 per cwt, with heavyweight choice up $2.29 at $105.13, USDA said. It reported 177 loads of fabricated beef sold.
